name: Ayase
tagline: Tokyo in 27 minutes and Otemachi in 27 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Adachi City, where JR East and Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 27 minutes to Otemachi, 38 minutes to Shinjuku, 48 minutes to Shibuya and 42 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 0 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 0 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.7 m to 0.1 m, a difference of 0.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 5 to 10 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: イトーヨーカドー 綾瀬店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 21 clinics and 18 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 東京拘置所医務部病院, about 18 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 健和会柳原病院, about 38 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: JR Joban Line and Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line and Tokyo Metro runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line runs at 150% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 町屋→西日暮里, which this station is not on. JR Joban Line runs at 142%. Its busiest stretch is 三河島→日暮里, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 2LDK ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. What holds the figure down: a large projected flood depth. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Aoi; for rail connections, Ayase.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Ayase in a straight line. Aoi has only the Tsukuba Express, so Ayase is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Aoi is 5 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥6,000 less at Aoi.

neighbours.lead: For how little of the area is in the flood projection, Kosuge; for rail connections, Ayase.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Ayase in a straight line. Kosuge has only the Tobu Skytree Line, so Ayase is the better connected. To Shinjuku, for instance, Kosuge takes 3 minutes longer. On safety, though, Kosuge comes out ahead.

goodFor: People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People living alone who want to hold the rent down
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The nearest big road, 江北橋通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
